title: UK regulators say personal AI agents do not remove company responsibility
dek: Four UK regulators have issued a joint statement on personal AI agents, telling developers to address authority, data use and redress under existing legal frameworks.

sources.title: Joint statement on protecting people and businesses in an agentic economy, October 30, 2026
Agentic AI and consumers: March 9 research and October 30 joint-statement update

lede: The CMA, FCA, ICO and Ofcom issued a joint statement on personal AI agents on October 30. They say companies remain responsible for legal compliance when software acts on a user’s behalf.

body.text: The statement asks developers and deploying firms to address how users grant an agent authority and understand its actions. It also covers personal-data use, commercial influences on recommendations, accountability for decisions and routes to redress. These questions apply to the surrounding product and business process, including how a user can resolve an unwanted transaction.
The regulators describe a coordinated approach under existing law. The CMA’s associated consumer research was first published in March; its October update links the new joint statement.

claims.text: The joint statement says autonomy does not reduce a deploying organization’s responsibility to comply with applicable law.
The statement introduces no new AI statute, single technical compliance standard or enforcement case against a named agent.

buildersNote: Assign an owner for agent permissions and complaints. Record what the user authorized and provide a route to challenge the resulting action.
